title: UruBots Autonomous Car Team Two: Team Description Paper for FIRA 2024
extended_summary:
This paper is not the requested education study on ChatGPT and academic writing. Instead, it is a team description paper for the 2024 FIRA Autonomous Cars Race Challenge. The paper addresses the design and readiness of a low-cost, lightweight mini autonomous car developed by the UruBots team for competition, focusing on autonomous navigation, hardware integration, and supervised learning for steering and speed control.

The approach centers on an RC-scale autonomous vehicle built with a Raspberry Pi 4, Logitech C270 camera, DC motors, servo steering, and supporting motor-control hardware. The software stack is based on the DonkeyCar platform, with custom configuration changes for the team’s hardware. The car is trained using supervised learning: camera images are recorded while a human drives the vehicle, and corresponding steering/throttle actions are logged in JSON format. A convolutional neural network based on the Keras Linear model is then trained on 1,500 samples for 60 epochs to predict steering angle and speed from visual input.

There is no human learner population, school setting, or educational intervention reported. The context is a robotics/autonomous vehicle competition setting at the Technological University of Uruguay - UTEC. The paper mainly describes the system architecture, components, training procedure, and vehicle characteristics rather than evaluating an educational outcome.

The authors conclude that the vehicle meets FIRA competition specifications and is capable of completing an approximately 13-meter track in 11 seconds at best evaluation, averaging about 1.2 m/s. They argue that the design is suitable for participation in the 2024 FIRA Autonomous Cars Race Challenge and contributes to development in autonomous vehicle research.
